text:
maria: ran a focused nsys trace on the 2048x1024 matmul regression. timeline shows repeated kernel relaunches and a bunch of small workspace alloc/free events that line up with latency spikes.

maria: sample heatmap: https://s3.redwood/nsys/1776004321/tile-heatmap.png :eyes:

ajay: can you paste the nsys cmd you used?

maria: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas --output=tile-sweep --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx` and then ran 10 warmup + 200 iters.

perf-bot: nsys summary: 1.2s cum time in cuBLAS calls, 64% in GEMM kernels, 18% in cuBLASLt workspace alloc/free.

oliver: interesting — does cuBLASLt choose different algos across tiles? maybe the stride pattern causes workspace fragmentation and it falls back.

sasha: saw something similar with KV cache churn — small varying sequence lengths cause matmul dims to jitter and cuBLASLt reconfigs. could be our batching heuristic.

maria: attached nvprof-style timeline snippet:

```
# timeline excerpt
GEMM_128x128_32b - 0.45ms
GEMM_256x128_32b - 0.47ms (relaunch + workspace alloc)
malloc/cudaFree - 0.12ms spikes coincident
```

ajay: try forcing cuBLASLt algo selection: `cublasLtMatmulPreferenceSetAttribute(..., CUBLASLT_MATMUL_PREF_MAX_WORKSPACE_BYTES, 1048576)` to cap workspace and see if it stabilizes.

oliver: or preallocate a workspace pool and use cublasLtMatmul with `workspace={pool_ptr, pool_size}` — avoids per-kernel alloc/free.

sasha: for batching, increase our tile grouping window to merge similar shapes before dispatch. reduces variety of algo choices.

maria: quick patch I ran:

```
// runtime change
engine->opts.batch_grouping.window_us = 5000;
engine->opts.kv_cache.pin_chunks = true; // reduce fragmentation
```

maria: that cut the median p50 by ~18% on the trace but p95 still had a tail.

ajay: p95 tail might be due to occasional sources of huge workspace requests from long prompts — can we add adaptive fallback to smaller algo on latency violations?

oliver: yes -> on-first-failure, mark shape->algo mapping in local cache to prefer low-workspace algos for that shape for next N mins.

perf-bot: ran a quick A/B sim: prealloc pool + grouping window -> reduced cuBLASLt workspace alloc/free events by 92% in synthetic trace.

sasha: can we add a perfetto trace for the next canary so we can see CPU-side scheduling and NVTX markers? nsys misses some CPU scheduling churn.

maria: good idea. I'll enqueue a canary with prealloc + grouping + algo-cache. perfetto capture + nsys parallel.

ajay: can you post the checklist for the canary? I'll own rolling it.

maria: checklist:
- deploy runtime build with prealloc pool flag
- enable batch_grouping.window_us=5000
- enable algo-cache TTL=10m
- run perfetto + nsys for 5k requests
- collect heatmap + kernel timelines

maria: assigning follow-up: @ajay to roll canary, @oliver to implement prealloc API cleanup, @sasha to add trace markers for kv-cache ops. :thumbsup:
